newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end up led by shipbuilders, stock firms.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end up led by shipbuilders, stock firms.

text.p: South Korean stocks recovered from early weakness to close Friday's session higher, led by shipbuilding and securities firms, brokers said.
Banks fell on expectations that deposit-taking competition would intensify among banks after interest rates on savings accounts are freed next week.
Samsung Aerospace Industries went limit-up on hopes that the company would benefit from the government's jet trainer aircraft development project.
The composite index closed up 6.44 points, or 0.83 percent, to 781.70.
Advancers led decliners by 401 to 361 and trading volume fell to 47.89 million shares from Thursday's 51.2 million.
All three listed shipbuilding companies rose sharply on news that foreign ship orders received during the first half of the year more than doubled from a year earlier.
Samsung Heavy Industries gained 800 won to its daily limit and yearly high of 11,400. Daewoo Heavy Industries closed up 570 won to 8,670 and Hanjin Heavy Industries up 280 won to 9,400.
Banks fell broadly, with the sector's sub-index losing 0.95 percent or 3.71 points to 387.97.
Securities firms gained on the belief that their earnings would improve in line with the overall stock market recovery from last year's slump.
But brokers said the falling trading volume reflected investor concern about the market's short-term prospects.
"The decreasing volume reflected a growing uncertainty among investors about the market's short-term course," said Kim Ik-hwan, a strategist at Hyundai Securities.
September index futures closed up 0.80 of a point to 85.30 while the underlying KOSPI-200 index up 0.99 to 82.38.
